w10_T4_011965: Sarah had 209 cents. She spent 2 cents on a pencil. Then she found 8 cents in a coat pocket. Her grandmother gave her 7 cents. She earned 4 cents for helping at home. Finally, she spent 68 cents, which converts to just under 1 dollar, on a small toy. Yesterday she saw a bike that cost 150 dollars but wasn't interested. How much money does Sarah have left in cents?
w10_T4_011970: A bookshelf started with 198 books. During spring cleanup, 166 books were donated to the library. Then Maya bought 78 used books from a garage sale. Later, 49 books were lent to a school, leaving them temporarily. Her family donated 68 books they found in the attic. Finally, 54 books were removed for recycling, and 16 new books were added. The living room had space for 200 more books (but that doesn't affect the count). How many books are on the bookshelf now?
w10_T4_011976: James collected 163 trading cards. He traded them with 4 other kids, giving each kid the same cards, so his collection was multiplied by 4. Then he found 73 new cards at a flea market. Afterward, he and his friend doubled their combined cards by trading—multiplied by 6. Finally, he organized all his cards into groups of 4. James' sister had a dozen rare cards but they weren't added to his collection. How many cards does James have in total?
w10_T4_011978: Maria started a savings fund with 112 dollars. She tripled her savings by picking up overtime shifts. Then her parents gave her 50 dollars as a gift. Her aunt sent another 80 dollars for her birthday. Maria then invested all her money, which grew ninefold by year-end. She divided the final amount equally among 3 college funds. What is the total amount in each fund?
w10_T4_012004: A grocery store had 171 apples on display. During the morning rush, 89 apples were sold to customers. At noon, 30 more apples were picked from the bin and sold. In the afternoon, 34 new apples arrived from the farm and were added to the display. Finally, 18 more apples were purchased by a restaurant. The store manager counted inventory for 45 minutes that morning (but that's separate from the apple count). How many apples were on the shelf at the end of the day?
w10_T4_011984: A farmer's chicken coop started with 79 eggs. Throughout the week, 75 eggs were laid. Then 48 eggs were collected for sale. After selling, 196 eggs were removed from the count due to them being sent to a market. Later, the hens laid 75 more eggs. Finally, 78 additional eggs arrived from a neighboring farm. A delivery truck carried 50 eggs from another farm (but these were not added). What was the total number of eggs the farmer had?
w10_T4_011985: A pizza restaurant had 233 frozen pizzas in stock. At lunch time, 55 pizzas were added to the freezer. Then the manager multiplied their total by 8 to prepare for a catering order. After filling the order, 34 pizzas remained and were logged. Finally, 1862 pizzas were sold over the course of a busy week (in hundreds of dollars in revenue). Jackson's rival restaurant had 300 pizzas but that's irrelevant to this store. How many pizzas are left in stock?
w10_T4_011987: Tom started learning guitar with 31 hours of free time. After joining lessons, 66 hours became available to practice. This 5-fold increase in his available practice time came from quitting a hobby. His practice time then doubled again by 5 times when he rearranged his schedule. Suddenly, 1974 hours of commitments appeared (in a hypothetical lifetime scenario). His commitment then multiplied by 5 when he took on a second job. Finally, he gained 70 additional hours of free time by vacation. His friend had 200 hours available but practices differently. How many total hours does Tom now have for practice, considering all increases and reductions?
w10_T4_011989: A theater had 176 seats. On opening night, 7 times that many tickets were sold (by mistake, selling 7 per seat category). Then 64 more reservations came in. During box office cleanup, 941 error reservations were removed from the system. Later, 69 legitimate bookings were added back. Finally, the theater multiplied available seating by 4 to account for future shows. Tom bought 50 tickets for a group but those are not counted separately. How many ticket slots are now available across all future shows?
w10_T4_011991: Maya started a knitting project with 192 yards of yarn. She used 75 yards to make a scarf. Then she cut off 84 yards for a different project. Later she found 20 yards of matching yarn and added it back. She discovered another 17 yards in a closet. Finally, she needed only 19 yards for her last piece, so she set that aside. Her sister had 40 yards of extra yarn but didn't contribute to Maya's pile. She divided her remaining yarn into 3 equal portions for three different projects. How many yards of yarn are in each portion?
w10_T4_011992: A classroom started with 131 pencils. The teacher added 66 new pencils from the supply closet. Then 128 broken pencils were removed and thrown away. She found 12 more pencils in a desk drawer. The class earned 33 bonus pencils from a school competition. Finally, the teacher removed 20 pencils for special art supplies and multiplied the remainder by 9 to create a "pencil pool" system. The principal bought 50 pencils for another classroom (not added to this count). How many pencils are now in the classroom pool?
w10_T4_011998: A toy store had 89 action figures on the shelf. A collector came in and bought 30 figures. The store then lost 105 figures in a warehouse mishap. They recovered 75 of those figures the next day. These recovered figures were then multiplied by 6 when they packaged them in cases of 6. The final batch was then multiplied by 3 to show how many figures could be sold in the next month. A store 50 miles away had 200 action figures in stock but that's not relevant here. How many action figures in total across all packages are expected to be sold?
w10_T4_011999: A runner started a race with 95 kilometers to cover. The first segment was 89 kilometers, which he successfully completed. He then divided the remaining distance in half, making 2 legs. He then multiplied the remaining leg by 4 to account for hills. The final stretch was half of that. His last dash covered 7 times that amount, and that was his final distance. A rival runner completed 50 kilometers but took a different route. How many kilometers did this runner cover in his final dash?
w10_T4_012008: A small town started with 42 people. Over the years, 68 new residents moved in. Then 72 more people arrived seeking jobs. After a factory closure, 162 residents left town. The town was then divided into 4 districts for administration. Each district was then given 4 community centers to manage. A neighboring town 100 miles away had 300 residents but operates independently. How many community centers does each district have?
w10_T4_012010: A library had 132 books on one shelf. The librarian added 53 more books. Then 72 additional volumes were donated by a local school. She shelved another 55 books from a clearance sale. Together, these books (132 + 53 + 72 + 55) totaled 312 books, which were then grouped into 6 themed collections. The total was reduced by 1454 books due to a library-wide reorganization that sent many to storage. Sarah had 200 books at home but those weren't part of the library. How many themed collections are now active in the library?
w10_T4_012012: A bakery started the day with 206 cookies. The baker tripled production, multiplying by 8. She added 69 more cookies from a special order. Then 5 more cookies were baked fresh. The display case held 56 cookies from the inventory. At close, 953 cookies were sold during the day (converting from cents to dollars, this was about $9.53). Finally, 8 broken cookies were discarded. The next-door café sold 150 cookies that day but they baked separately. How many cookies does the bakery have left?
w10_T4_012016: A farmer started with 37 sheep in one pasture. He added 45 sheep to double the group. The flock grew by 6 times that new amount in the spring breeding season. Then it multiplied by 5 more due to additional births. Finally, it multiplied by 8 times again as he combined herds. He added 16 more sheep at the end of the week. A neighboring farm had 200 sheep but kept separate grazing areas. How many sheep are in the combined pasture now?
w10_T4_012021: A student earned 134 points in the first round of a competition. She gained 62 points in the second round. Then she earned 30 additional points in a bonus round. She lost 27 points for a small mistake. She regained 50 points from an appeals decision. Her score was then multiplied by 3 for the final calculation. Her classmate scored 180 points but in a different division. What is the student's final multiplied score?
w10_T4_012024: An aquarium had 140 fish initially. During a sale, 28 fish were sold to customers. The owner then acquired 19 more fish from a supplier. He found 3 fish had escaped, reducing the count. Later, 67 fish were removed for a transfer to another tank. Finally, he bought 40 new exotic fish to add to the main display. The store down the street had 80 fish but they're not counted here. How many fish are now in the aquarium?
w10_T4_012026: A company started with 76 employees. The team grew to 5 times that size when hired for a major project. Then they multiplied by 4 again for a second wave of hiring. The operation multiplied by 6 to reflect the scaled-up office. After restructuring, 4075 positions were eliminated due to automation. Then, in a rare expansion, they multiplied by 5 again. Finally, they divided by 5 to normalize departments, converting hundreds of dollars of payroll to new budgets. A rival company had 2000 employees but that's separate. How many employees does the company now have?
w10_T4_012033: A gardener planted 147 flowers. She removed 139 to replant them in rows. She divided the remaining flowers into 4 groups for different beds. She then multiplied one group by 3 to increase the planting density. She multiplied again by 3 for a hedge garden. Finally, she added 17 more small seedlings to that bed. The park nearby had a dozen beautiful gardens but not relevant to her count. How many flowers are in the hedge garden?
w10_T4_012034: Maya had 45 cookies and wanted to package them. She tripled the batch by mixing in ingredients. She divided by 5 to make smaller portions. She then multiplied by 8 for a gift box. She multiplied by another 8 to fill multiple boxes. Finally, she added 65 more cookies for a party. Her neighbor baked 100 cookies separately (not combined). How many cookies did Maya end up with for the party?
w10_T4_012035: A warehouse had 209 boxes. Two boxes disappeared (minus 3). The manager multiplied the remaining count by 6 to forecast stock for the quarter. She added 28 more boxes that arrived. Then, due to an error, 1135 boxes were listed but later found to be a system glitch. She added 47 boxes back after the audit. A delivery truck from 50 miles away had 500 boxes but didn't contribute to this warehouse. How many boxes should be in the corrected warehouse count?
w10_T4_012037: A school had 52 computers in the lab. The IT team tripled the number by acquiring donations. She added 14 more functional machines. Then the collection multiplied by 8 through a grant purchase. The lab then split the machines in half between two school buildings. How many computers does each building receive?
